description: Hi! We are a team that loves nature, farming and science. We want to create a tool that helps farmers choose the best crops to grow and take care of their soil. We are looking for friends who enjoy science, technology, coding, designing and solving problems. Let's share our ideas, learn about farming and use technology to help farmers and protect our planet!
summary: We have made a scratch project which simulates the  person who is using it as a farmer. This farmer connects environmental indicators such as rainfall, temperature, and more with NASA's data. This project creates a result (a crop to plant) based on the conditions and environmental factors the farm is going through.
details:
FIELD SHIFT - NASA SPACE APPS CHALLENGE 2026

We built a Scratch simulation where the person steps into the shoes of a farmer.

That farmer matches local weather metrics like rain, heat, and more with NASA datasets. The program delivers an output (a crop to grow) tailored to the exact conditions and environmental factors the land is facing.

The benefits that this project has is helping farmers get data from NASA datasets to improve farms and make them grow. The impact of this project was changing lives and turning them around by getting more food, making farms grow, and developing the agriculture of India.

We have used Scratch to program our project, Canva to show the slides of the ppt, AI for backgrounds and images, and other agriculture sites such as Times of India and Indian Express.

Our project is unique because unlike other projects which give the NASA data directly, we create a result from variables and conditions. One major factor our team considered was creating a result using our variable system.

We did did this by counting scores of each condition- month, temperature, soil quality, rainfall, and the previous crop grown to determine the final crop to grow next. This works by permutation combinations, like all variables are first set to 0 then it goes to the location page, which shows East India, Maharashtra, and North India which are locations 1, 2, and 3 respectively. So if you pick North India the location goes to three. After that the backdrop switches to picking a month, which is January - 1, February - 2, March - 3, and so on till December - 12. Then, you pick June, which makes the month variable 6. Now the backdrop switches to temperature, which is low medium, high all 1, 2, and 3 respectively. If you pick medium the temperature variable goes to 2. Then the backdrop switches to soil quality, which shows the soil based on the location. Since you picked north India the soil quality's are clay, arid (desert soil), and alluvial soil all 3, 2, 1 respectively. Let's say you pick clay soil which makes the soil quality variable 3. Then the backdrop switches to rainfall which is like temperature - low, medium and high which is 1, 2, and 3. Now let's say you pick high, now the rainfall variable is at 3. Then the second last page which has all the crops based on the location and you have to pick the crop you planted in the previous month, which your previous month is may. Now in north India in May the crop that is grown is chickpea so you click that. And there is your result for the crop you have to grow in June (Rice) with the conditions you have.

Thank You
